newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Promstroibank to issue Eurobond in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Promstroibank to issue Eurobond in 1997.

text.p: One of Russia's biggest banks, Sankt-Peterburgsky Promyshlenno-Stroitelny Bank (Promstroibank) plans to issue a Eurobond in 1997, the bank's chairman David Traktovenko said on Monday.
He told Reuters that CS First Boston was working with the bank on the project.
The volume and date of the issue will be set by the bank's Council.
In 1996 the BankWatch rating agency awarded Promstroibank IC-D/LC-3 international rating.
Promstroibank shareholders decided at their meeting on April 24 to raise the bank's authorised capital to 99.3 billion roubles from two billion roubles.
In 1997 Promstroibank made a new 700 million rouble share issue, raising the capital to two billion roubles.
Promstroibank also gave the following data for its 1996 results.
Year ending December 31 (billion roubles):
Pre-tax profit 329.0 332.5
Shareholders' capital 792.8 329.6
NOTE - Figures to Russian accounting standards. Peterburgbank audited the figures to Russian accounting standards, Price Waterhouse to international standards.

Russian accounting standards differ significantly from those normally supplied in the West. Russian accounts are designed to meet the requirements of the tax authorities. Russian companies can choose whether to show revenues and spending on a cash or accruals basis, but it was not clear on what basis Promstroibank's results were reported. Definitions of profit and assets differ significantly from those in the West, and converting Russian accounts to international standards can turn a profit into a loss.
